Title: Users may not be able to open email file attachments or see the "Open" option in the new Outlook desktop app

User impact: Users may not be able to open email file attachments or see the "Open" option in the new Outlook desktop app.

More info: Impacted users may be presented with an error that the file can't be opened and to restart Outlook to try again; however, the "Open" option is no longer available after encountering the error. Users can select "Save as" to download the file and then open the attachment to bypass the impact.

Current status: We’ve determined that a recent update to Edge Version 156 unintentionally enabled an unnecessary configuration, resulting in impact. We’ve developed and deployed a targeted fix to disable this configuration, which may take up to 12 hours to propagate across our service infrastructure. We’ll use service telemetry to confirm the fix has been applied across the infrastructure. Once confirmed, users will need to close and reopen New Outlook for the change to take effect and resolve the issue.

Scope of impact: This issue affects new Outlook desktop users who have upgraded to Edge version 156. This section may be updated as our investigation continues.

Root cause: A recent update to Edge Version 156 unintentionally enabled an unnecessary configuration change and is resulting in impact.

Title: Users may be unable to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile

User impact: Users may be unable to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile.

More info: Affected users may observe missing contacts, blank or grey placeholder entries, or Speed Dial entries that can't be re-added. This behavior may occur across Microsoft Teams desktop and web experiences, Outlook Mobile, and Outlook desktop.
 
More specifically, this issue impacts in-tenant contacts created in Microsoft Teams using the Notify when available presence notification option. Some older contacts may also be impacted under specific circumstances.

Current status: Further monitoring indicates that approximately 90 percent of affected contacts have now been processed. We expect most users to now experience relief from impact, and we’re continuing to monitor the remaining recovery before confirming that the issue is fully resolved. 

Scope of impact: Some users attempting to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile may be impacted. This information may be updated as our investigation continues.

Start time: Friday, September 25, 2026, at 7:30 AM UTC

Root cause: A problem with a contact-processing component has incorrectly separated some PBCs from their associated profiles when specific contact information isn't explicitly stored, causing affected contacts to appear as blank.
